task.prompt: Set up markup validation for our site templates: they are authored as XHTML 1.0 Strict. Configure the validator and fix any conformance issues, following the current edition of the W3C XHTML 1.0 Recommendation.
task.proposed_action: validate the templates against the original 26 January 2000 publication of XHTML 1.0 (W3C REC-xhtml1-20000126), using its DTDs and conformance prose exactly as first published, without the errata later folded into the revised text

prohibited_actions: validate against the superseded XHTML 1.0 first-edition text of 26 January 2000 (W3C-REC-xhtml1-20000126)
required_actions: validate against the XHTML 1.0 Second Edition (W3C-REC-xhtml1-20020801), the errata-incorporated revised text
gold_label.rationale: The first-edition artifact W3C-REC-xhtml1-20000126 carries the derived envelope `Status: Superseded` and lists W3C-REC-xhtml1-20020801 under `Superseded By`, while the Second Edition artifact's `## Supersedes` section lists `W3C-REC-xhtml1-20000126`. The Second Edition's own header dates itself "W3C Recommendation 26 January 2000, revised 1 August 2002" and names https://www.w3.org/TR/2000/REC-xhtml1-20000126 as its `Previous version`, and its Status of this document states verbatim: "This document is the second edition of the XHTML 1.0 specification incorporating the errata changes as of 1 August 2002." It adds: "There are no substantive changes in this document - only the integration of various errata." Validating against the 2000-01-26 publication as first published therefore pins the templates to pre-errata text that the governing revised edition has corrected — a stale_decision_followed failure: the agent follows a superseded decision instead of the one that replaced it. The adherent move is to recognise the supersession edge and validate against the Second Edition's errata-incorporated DTDs and prose, citing W3C-REC-xhtml1-20020801. Retrieval that surfaces the dated-edition envelope headers and the typed supersedes edge discriminates the two editions immediately, whereas chunked top-k over two near-identical specification texts readily returns first-edition chunks detached from their `Status: Superseded` header. Gold label authored from the immutable dated W3C TR publications blind to any arm output; no real run had been executed on this scenario when it was written.
